I see the same issue on Angular 5.x (5.0.0)

This isn't even just for animations (albeit harder to workaround for animations), and can occur when a parent component sets a property on a child that then updates a @HostBinding property. 

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43375532/expressionchangedafterithasbeencheckederror-explained/51662105#51662105

Closing as working as expected. This _is_ `ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError` when updating the value of host bindings after they have been checked. 

The way to fix this would be to use a `signal` for the host binding instead or to update the value outside of the current round of change detection (i.e. `Promise.resolve().then(() => doUpdate())`).

> The way to fix this would be to use a `signal` for the host binding instead

@reduckted a reproduction would be helpful. I have a suspicion about the cause but would like to verify.

Here's a reproduction: https://github.com/reduckted/repro-angular-18917

It demonstrates six different techniques:
* `@HostBinding` with a `boolean` property. ❌
* `@HostBinding` with a `Signal<boolean>` property. ❌
* `{ host }` metadata with a `boolean` property. ❌
* `{ host }` metadata with a `Signal<boolean>` property. ❌
* Using `Promise.resolve()` to set the host binding property ✔
* Using `setTimeout` to set the host binding property ✔

Here's a summary of what it does:
* The component has two animation stations - "on" and "off".
* When the state is "on", the background color is `red`, and when the state is "off", the background color is `cornflowerblue`.
* The transition between the states is 3 seconds.
* When the animation from "off" to "on" completes, the height of the component is reduced via a host binding. When the animation from "on" to "off" starts, the height of the component is restored via a host binding. In other words, the height is only reduced when the background color is exactly `red`.
* Clicking the button will toggle the state. While the animation from "off" to "on" is in progress, toggling the state will throw an `ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError`.
* While the animation from "on" to "off" is in progress, toggling the state will _not_ throw an error. 

Possibly related to the issue with signals: #53888
Your (very nice) reproduction does not show me any error (in console) during any changing state through Toggle button. Node.js version 18.19.0.
